assigned.title: Corrective, re-run: production rights-invariant breach in the watch route
assigned.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0703 and carries the same corrective forward under an honest review range. PL-0703 recorded implementationBaseSha f6c4b942ebbd02fd3fa9ed8f74fde4fc603affc2, which opened its review range AFTER part of the implementation already existed: the first incident repair at 9933a55 falls before that base and was therefore excluded from the range the first review was bound to. That record cannot be repaired in place. release is reachable only from CLAIMED or IN_PROGRESS and PL-0703 is in REVIEW; release deliberately PRESERVES implementationBaseSha even when it is usable; and reconciliation refuses any task that already records a base, because reconciliation establishes a base rather than revising one. The prescribed remedy is therefore to BLOCK PL-0703, preserving the false narrowed base as audit history, and to run the work again here. THIS TASK'S OWN BASE MUST BE RECONCILED, not captured: claim it, then start it with --reconcile-existing --base cf98b977b3c7c0113928bb9cc4d7fb6d02e802bd. That sha is the true pre-implementation base, being the immediate parent of the first incident-repair commit. Do NOT use its own parent b0b1dcf5a4826b763aa72d6375dd93e95a3aff33, which would widen the asserted range by one unrelated commit and make implementationBaseSha false in the other direction. The allowedPaths below are PL-0703's declared set plus packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/** and packages/provider-sdk/src/index.ts, because this round's corrective collapsed the two fixture providers onto the SDK's one and therefore writes there. The reviewDependencies carry over e2e/tests/media-rig.spec.ts and add e2e/src/env.ts and e2e/src/fixtures.ts: WEB_MODE and MANAGES_SERVER in the first decide the production-versus-development assertion, and TINY_DEVICE in the second is the probe that makes the unknown-height regression meaningful, so an approval that did not fingerprint them would stay artificially fresh after someone altered the mode classifier or the probe. packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/** is deliberately NOT also listed as a reviewDependency: it is a write path here, allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface, and the validator warns on the redundancy.
assigned.notes: NOT ONLY A PROVENANCE REWRITE. At the previous head the reviewer refused BOTH security-review and rights-review ON THE MERITS, and those refusals are the substantive work this task inherits: the corrective had not reduced the fixture providers to one with the application consuming the SDK's, the runtime allowlist was not expressed exactly once with the SDK holding a witness it can neither forge nor classify for itself, the opaque rights-reference rule still existed in more than one place, a fabricated rights basis remained reachable behind a deletable condition rather than being structurally unconstructible in a deployment environment, and the two Playwright modes were not both shown as EXECUTED. PL-0703's typecheck, unit and e2e passes belong to that abandoned round and do not carry over; every gate here is re-recorded under this task's owner. ALLOWEDPATHS WIDENED BY EXACTLY ONE LEAF, packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, for the construction boundary the reviewer refused on. gpt-architect withheld security-review and rights-review in this round's review because the SDK's construction boundary is still forgeable: RuntimeClassification is a public STRUCTURAL interface carrying only nodeEnv, packages/provider-sdk/src/index.ts exports both it and createFixtureProvider, and createFixtureProvider mints its nominal NonProductionRuntime witness from whatever structural object it is handed -- so any caller can pass an object literal from a production process and obtain a real FixtureRightsBasis. fixture/environment.ts concedes the point in its own header: a literal satisfies it too. The prescription was a single NOMINAL runtime capability at a LOWER SHARED BOUNDARY that both the app and the SDK consume, with exactly one place performing the classification; a second duplicated allowlist and any weakening of this task's acceptance were both explicitly refused. No such boundary is reachable from the paths already declared here. apps/web/src/app/api/deployment-environment.ts is imported by five non-test modules under apps/web/src/lib/** that this task does not own -- session/account.ts, demo-catalog.ts, catalog-source-registry.ts, db/index.ts and db/in-memory-repository.ts -- so relocating it is not this task's to do; and routing the classification through @liberty/provider-sdk is worse, because that package publishes a single root entry point (exports is the bare string ./src/index.ts) and would drag the whole provider SDK into the module graph of every surface that renders a catalog card. @liberty/contracts is already a declared dependency of BOTH apps/web and packages/provider-sdk, and its exports map already carries a ./shared/* wildcard that apps/web, media-engine and recommendations import through today, so a new leaf module there needs no manifest, workspace, tsconfig or turbo change. Every path, edge and export named in this paragraph was read out of the tree rather than taken on report. The declaration is the single leaf file rather than packages/contracts/**, because that is the narrowest surface that admits the fix. SEQUENCING, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: PL-0203 declares packages/contracts/** and is still active, and pathsOverlap tests prefix containment in EITHER direction, so this leaf collides with PL-0203 exactly as the wide prefix would. ai:validate reports an active write-path conflict between PL-0203 and PL-0706 until PL-0203 leaves CLAIMED/IN_PROGRESS/REVIEW, so PL-0203's approval and completion have to land before this widening is validated. WIDENED A SECOND TIME, BY FOUR INDIVIDUAL FILES AND DELIBERATELY NOT BY apps/web/src/lib/**: a glob over that directory would contain PL-0105's own apps/web/src/lib/catalog-source.ts and catalog-source-registry.ts and collide with an active task, whereas apps/web/src/lib/demo-catalog.ts, apps/web/src/lib/db/index.ts, apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.ts and apps/web/src/lib/session/account.ts are prefix-disjoint from every path PL-0105 declares as a write surface; each of those four documents the environment gate in its header and none of them could keep describing it accurately once the allowlist and the capability moved out of apps/web into packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, and this repository treats a false comment as a defect, so correcting all four is part of this same change rather than follow-up -- which supersedes the sentence above stating the widening is exactly one leaf. DECLARATION GAP CLOSED, THIRD WIDENING, TWO FILES, AND ONE OF THEM IS A MOVE BETWEEN SURFACES. (1) e2e/src/fixtures.ts MOVED from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths. reviewDependencies is read-only by contract and this file was EDITED this round, so leaving it there was a real violation rather than a bookkeeping nicety: no collision check had reserved it, and the description's paragraph above -- which argues fixtures.ts belongs on the read-only surface for TINY_DEVICE -- was written before this round's edit and is superseded here rather than deleted. The edit is unmistakably this task's: the DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_HEADER commentary now states that NonDeploymentEnvironment 'is not a class and has no constructor of any kind: it is a branded value, minted only by classifyRuntime in @liberty/contracts/shared/runtime, whose brand key is a unique symbol that module never exports' -- it names the module this task created and explicitly retracts the private-constructor witness this task replaced. It is NOT also left as a reviewDependency, because allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface and the validator warns on that redundancy; the approval still fingerprints it. (2) docs/API_CONTRACTS.md added to allowedPaths: its storage-selection section was corrected to the same new fact, now reading that createInMemoryRepository requires the branded capability classifyRuntime issues in @liberty/contracts/shared/runtime, 'not a class, and with no constructor at all', with the allowlist 'declared there and nowhere else'. That is this task's correction of a claim this task falsified, and product invariant 5 makes the contracts doc part of the change rather than a follow-up. FUTURE COLLISION, RECORDED DELIBERATELY: PL-0601 also declares docs/API_CONTRACTS.md and is READY and unowned, so no active write-path conflict exists today and ai:validate is unaffected. It was declared here anyway because the alternative -- leaving a rights-relevant correction outside every declared surface -- is the exact defect this record exists to prevent, and because the collision it creates is not a new one: PL-0601 also declares packages/contracts/**, which already prefix-contains this task's packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and already overlaps PL-0203's and PL-0206's packages/contracts/**. PL-0601 is therefore already unclaimable while this task is active, and adding a second overlapping entry to an already-overlapping pair changes neither validate's verdict nor dispatch's. Sequence PL-0601 after this task and PL-0203, as the paragraph above already requires. NOT DECLARED, AND THE OMISSION IS THE FINDING: apps/web/src/lib/db/index.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts and apps/web/src/lib/session/account.test.ts were reported as changed by this round's runtime-capability move and were NOT. Each was read: none asserts a private constructor, none states where the allowlist lives, and none names classifyRuntime -- they speak of 'the witness' and 'the exported allowlist', wording that survived the move unaltered, which is precisely why app/api/deployment-environment.ts kept its re-export line and its NonDeploymentEnvironment.classify shape ('so the app's own suites can keep importing the set from the module they already import the classification from'). Their on-disk modification times sit in the earlier persistence-wiring round beside db/request-context.ts and db/reason-trail.ts, well before this round's cluster. Declaring an unchanged file would pad the review range as surely as omitting a changed one narrows it, so all three were declined. COLLISION-CHECKED BEFORE ADDING: e2e/src/fixtures.ts and docs/API_CONTRACTS.md are prefix-disjoint from every allowedPaths entry of the other active tasks -- PL-0104 and PL-0105 (claude-frontend), PL-0203 (claude-media), PL-AI-0005 (claude-lead) -- including PL-0105's newly declared sibling e2e/src/env.ts, which is neither a prefix of e2e/src/fixtures.ts nor contained by it, and PL-AI-0005's newly declared docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and docs/GITHUB_SETUP.md. No second active conflict is created; the only one remains PL-0203 versus this task over packages/contracts. FOURTH WIDENING, SIX TEST FILES, AND IT SUPERSEDES THE DECLINE RECORDED ABOVE: this corrective took the environment-name parameter off the mint, so every suite that used to obtain a capability by naming an environment had to be rewritten to call the parameterless classify() and handle its null, and those rewrites are part of this change rather than follow-up -- apps/web/src/lib/db/index.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/session/account.test.ts, apps/web/src/app/api/v1/profiles/handler.test.ts, apps/web/src/app/api/v1/watchlist/handler.test.ts and apps/web/src/app/api/v1/progress/handler.test.ts. Each was re-read before being declared: all six call NonDeploymentEnvironment.classify() with no argument and branch on the null, the first three narrate the removal in their own headers ('It used to pass a nodeEnv string, so one loop over a list of names could exercise both branches at once -- which was exactly the hole the corrective closed'), and the last three hand the resulting witness to createInMemoryRepository, which now takes it. Wording that could only have been written after the mint changed is direct evidence of an edit made after the paragraph above declined the first three as unchanged, so that decline is superseded on the facts rather than reversed on report; padding a review range is the same defect as narrowing one, and nothing is declared here without that evidence. COLLISION-CHECKED BEFORE ADDING: the active set is PL-AI-0005 (claude-lead), PL-0105 (claude-frontend) and this task (claude-security), and all six entries are prefix-disjoint in BOTH directions from every allowedPaths entry of the other two -- PL-0105's apps/web/src/lib/catalog-source.ts and catalog-source-registry.ts and their tests, app/search/**, app/title/demo-title-details.ts, app/api/v1/catalog/home/**, docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md and e2e/src/env.ts contain none of them and are contained by none, and PL-AI-0005 declares only scripts paths and two docs. apps/web/** is declared by PL-0701 (BACKLOG) and PL-AI-0006 (READY), both unowned and both already prefix-containing this task's existing apps/web entries, so no new active conflict is created and validate's verdict is unchanged. Nor are the six redundant with this task's own db/index.ts, db/in-memory-repository.ts and session/account.ts: a .ts path is not a prefix of its .test.ts sibling.
assigned.acceptance: Exactly ONE fixture provider exists in the repository, and the application CONSUMES the provider-sdk's rather than implementing its own: no route, no API handler and no watch-surface module declares a rights basis, composes a media URL, invents a candidate id or carries its own copy of the fixture variants. The runtime allowlist that decides which environments may construct fixtures is expressed ONCE by the application, and the SDK holds a witness it can neither forge nor classify for itself, so the SDK cannot admit itself into a deployment. The opaque rights-reference rule exists in exactly ONE place, with every other consumer importing it rather than restating it. A fabricated rights basis is structurally UNCONSTRUCTIBLE in a deployment environment -- unreachable because no constructor can be reached without the application-issued witness -- rather than guarded by a condition that deleting one line would remove. Both Playwright modes, production and development, are EXECUTED rather than only typechecked, and the gate evidence names the run, the commit and the per-mode results.

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck plus npm run check, plus the standalone e2e tsc pass, exit 0 under pinned Node 22 on the tree committed this round. classifyRuntime now declares no parameter and reads the process itself, so there is no argument for a caller to write; allowlist names are covered by a separate pure predicate that mints nothing. Every call site that previously named an environment -- both catalog registry accessors, search, the title fixture source, the repository selector, the development account and six test suites -- now takes capability-or-null.

unit.evidence: vitest via npm run check, exit 0 on the tree committed this round. Four consumers that previously accepted the capability's TYPE alone -- demoCatalogSource, selectRepository, createInMemoryRepository and developmentAccount -- now call isClassifiedRuntime as their first action, and each has a forgery test covering the two things a compile-time brand cannot stop: an as-cast, and a spread copy of a genuine capability, which type-checks with no cast at all and is rejected only by object identity. The reviewer deferred widening those three; they were widened anyway, because two acceptance fields claim the fixtures are unconstructible in a deployment and that claim was not true while the type alone was the gate.

e2e.evidence: Playwright executed in BOTH modes against the tree committed this round, after the capability mint stopped accepting a caller-supplied runtime name: production and development both exited 0 across chromium, firefox, webkit and mobile-safari. This supersedes the record that pointed at ed5d11d5, which gpt-architect identified as describing a run other than the one it was bound to. The specs assert on candidate ids and media URIs composed by the SDK's fixture provider, which now obtains its capability from the process rather than from an argument, so this is evidence about the corrected construction path rather than a repeat of an earlier result.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: PL-0706 supersedes PL-0703, whose implementationBaseSha was recorded by an ordinary start at f6c4b942 and therefore excluded the first incident repair at 9933a55. gpt-architect verified that defect cannot be repaired in place -- release is unavailable from REVIEW and preserves an existing base, and reconciliation refuses a task that already records one -- and prescribed a blocked predecessor plus a reconciled successor. This base is cf98b977b3c7c0113928bb9cc4d7fb6d02e802bd, the immediate parent of 9933a55, named by the reviewer after reading the commit graph. It is deliberately NOT b0b1dcf5a4826b763aa72d6375dd93e95a3aff33, cf98b977's own parent, which is the unrelated PL-0503/PL-0504 commit and would widen the asserted implementation range by one commit that does not belong to this incident. The window, both endpoints and the base commit's own surface touches are published for the reviewer to confirm.

review.evidence: CHANGES_REQUESTED on security-review and rights-review because the new brand, freeze and WeakSet correctly reject structural literals, casts and spread copies, but the public classifyRuntime capability mint still accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied nodeEnv, so production code can call it with test and receive a genuine identity-registered capability that createFixtureProvider accepts. The registry therefore proves only that the shared module issued the object, not that the classification describes the running process, leaving the central construction authority caller-controlled one level earlier. The single allowlist, single fixture provider, SDK identity check, URL refusal ordering, opaque rights rule and candidate-id contract are otherwise sound. Make the production mint observe the process boundary without a caller-selectable runtime name and keep test injection downstream of that authority boundary. The currently recorded PL-0706 e2e gate still points to ed5d11d5 rather than the reported post-rewrite execution, so after this correction the two-mode Playwright run must be executed again and the machine gate superseded with evidence bound to the corrected tree. Reviewed at 9bd95543eb40796e9b5f91aaf986671b3d064c7d. TRANSCRIBED BY CLAUDE from the ChatGPT review session; the GitHub write integration returns 403.

reviewHistory.evidence: CHANGES_REQUESTED on both security-review and rights-review because the provider SDK still accepts a public structural RuntimeClassification and publicly exports createFixtureProvider, so any consumer can supply a literal nonblank nodeEnv and cause the factory to mint the nominal runtime witness and fabricated fixture rights basis without an application-issued classification. The single allowlist and single fixture implementation are real improvements, the construction-time URL refusal is correctly surfaced as provider unavailable without echoing credentials, the opaque reference remains non-semantic, the corrected E2E path passed in both modes, and preserving the existing candidate-id wire shape is appropriate, but the central structural-unconstructibility claim is not yet true. Reviewed at f0e1546a74e8b7632ab5549e4dea7d762bcf73da; this record binds to the later commit because request-changes cannot bind to a sha whose reviewed surface has since changed.
